The Norns are three ancient beings whose names are Urd, Verdandi, and Skuld. They weave and guard the fates of all things, and they are older and more powerful than the gods themselves. Even Odin cannot escape the destinies they spin.

Each Norn represents a different aspect of time. Urd embodies the past—what has become. Verdandi embodies the present—what is becoming. Skuld embodies the future—what shall become. Together they hold all moments in their hands. They dwell at the Well of Urd, the sacred spring at the base of Yggdrasil where they daily water and tend the World Tree. In doing so, they maintain the very structure of existence.

The Norns are older and more fundamental than the gods themselves. They are beings of creation rather than created beings, suggesting they existed before the universe we know was shaped. They spin and weave the threads of fate for gods, humans, giants, and all creatures that exist. Their decisions are absolute and cannot be changed even by divine power. Odin consults them but cannot control them. Even the All-Father must accept the fates they have woven, including his own death at Ragnarok.

The Norns carve runes and symbols into the bark of Yggdrasil, encoding the patterns of destiny into the very structure of existence itself. This is their ultimate power—not merely to know what will come, but to inscribe it into the substance of the World Tree. They represent the paradox that all things, even gods, are subject to forces greater than themselves. Balder's death, foreseen by the Norns, could not be prevented even to save the brightest of the gods. The Norns exist in the world created from Ymir's body, ancient guardians of a cosmos built from primordial sacrifice.
